Gently round each piece into a loose ball by dragging it towards you on an unfloured part of the table, so the bottom grips and the top tightens. Cover and leave for 15 to 20 minutes. This **bench rest** relaxes the gluten, so the final shaping is easy and the dough does not tear.
Final shapes

items: **Round (boule):** fold the edges to the centre, flip seam down, then drag and rotate until the surface is tight and smooth.
**Oval (batard):** flatten to a rectangle, fold the top third down and the bottom third up, then roll and seal the seam firmly with the heel of your hand.
**Tin loaf:** shape as a batard the length of the tin, or roll up tightly like a mat, and place seam down in a greased tin.
**Rolls:** cup your hand over a small piece and rotate on the table until a tight ball forms.

blocks.title: Is it ready to bake?
items: Grown clearly in size
Poke springs back slowly
Small dent remains
Surface smooth, not tearing
Oven fully preheated
blocks.caption: If the poke springs back fast it needs more time; if it does not spring back at all it has over-proofed.

blocks.text: The poke test

Flour a fingertip and press about 1 cm into the side of the proofing dough. **Underproofed:** springs back quickly; the loaf will burst open unevenly. **Ready:** springs back slowly and leaves a small dent. **Over-proofed:** stays dented and the dough feels fragile; it may collapse when scored. In a hot room final proof can be fast, so start checking early.

Where you proof matters too. Cover shaped dough with an upturned clean bowl, a lightly oiled sheet of plastic or a large clean bag so the surface does not dry and form a skin. In a hot kitchen, proof away from the cooker and direct sun, and consider moving loaves into the fridge for part of the proof if your oven is still busy with another batch.
Scoring and steam

Scoring is a quick cut in the surface just before baking. It controls where the loaf expands, so it opens neatly instead of bursting at the side. Use a razor blade on a holder (called a lame) or a very sharp small knife. Cut with confidence in one smooth stroke, about 0.5 to 1 cm deep. For an ear on a batard, hold the blade at a low angle, around 30 degrees, rather than straight down.

Steam in the first 10 to 15 minutes keeps the crust soft long enough for the loaf to expand fully, and gives a glossy, crisp crust. In a home oven you can bake inside a preheated heavy lidded pot, removing the lid after about 20 minutes, or place a metal tray on the lowest shelf while the oven heats and pour in a cup of hot water as the bread goes in. Bake lean loaves hot, often around 220 to 240 C.

blocks.title: Steam burns
blocks.text: Steam burns as badly as boiling water. Pour water into the hot tray with a long-handled jug, keep your face and arms back, and wear dry oven gloves. Never use a glass dish for steam; cold water can shatter hot glass. Open the oven door slowly and stand to one side.

takeaways: Divide by weight and allow for your own bake loss.
Pre-shape, rest 15 to 20 minutes, then shape with tension.
Ready dough springs back slowly and leaves a small dent.
Score 0.5 to 1 cm deep in one stroke and bake with steam.

activity.title: Shape and score three loaves
steps: Weigh three pieces of dough to the same weight.
Shape one boule, one batard and one tin loaf.
Use the poke test to decide when each is ready, and record the times.
Score and bake with steam; weigh each baked loaf to calculate your bake loss.
activity.evidence: Photos of the shaped and baked loaves, and your bake loss calculation for each.

lessons.title: Enriched breads: brioche and tangzhong milk bread
objectives: Explain how butter, eggs, milk and sugar change a dough
Mix a brioche dough by adding butter after gluten is developed
Make a tangzhong and use it in a soft milk bread formula
Bake and store enriched breads so they stay soft

blocks.text: An **enriched dough** contains fat, sugar, eggs or milk on top of flour, water, yeast and salt. These ingredients tenderise the crumb, soften the crust, add flavour and help the bread stay soft for longer. Soft sweet bread is hugely popular in Nigeria, and a well made brioche or milk bread can sell at a premium in bakeries, cafes and on WhatsApp orders. But enrichment also makes dough slower and stickier, so the method changes.

blocks.name: glass-of-milk
blocks.caption: Milk, butter and eggs turn a lean dough into soft, rich bread.

blocks.title: Lean versus enriched dough
items: Lean dough
Enriched dough
blocks.caption: Enrichment changes the mixing, the rise time and the baking temperature.

blocks.text: Brioche: the richest dough

items: Mix flour, eggs, milk, sugar, salt and yeast until the dough is smooth and passes a good windowpane test. This takes longer than lean dough; a mixer helps a lot.
Add the butter a small piece at a time, mixing until each is absorbed. The dough will look broken, then come back together glossy and smooth.
Keep the dough cool: if it rises above about 26 C the butter softens and the dough turns greasy. Stop and chill the bowl if needed.
Bulk ferment about 1 hour, then fold, cover and refrigerate overnight. Cold brioche is much easier to shape.
Shape cold, proof until about doubled and very soft, egg wash gently and bake at about 180 C until deep golden. A large loaf is done at about 88 to 90 C in the centre.

blocks.text: Tangzhong: the secret of soft milk bread

**Tangzhong** is a cooked paste of flour and liquid, usually **1 part flour to 5 parts water or milk**, heated while stirring until it thickens to about 65 C. The heat swells the starch so it holds much more water. Added to dough, it gives a very soft, moist, feathery crumb that stays soft for several days. Many bakers use flour equal to about 5 to 10% of the total flour for the tangzhong.

blocks.title: Worked example: a tangzhong milk loaf formula
blocks.context: For example, Folake in Abeokuta wants a soft milk loaf for a cafe. She plans 500 g total flour and uses 5% of it for the tangzhong.
steps: Tangzhong flour: 500 x 5% = 25 g. Liquid at 1 : 5: 25 x 5 = 125 g milk. She cooks them to 65 C and cools the paste.
Remaining flour for the dough: 500 - 25 = 475 g bread flour.
Dough liquids: 175 g milk and 1 egg (50 g). Total liquid including tangzhong = 125 + 175 + 50 = 350 g, which is 70% of 500 g: a soft, slightly sticky dough.
She adds 50 g sugar (10%), 8 g salt (1.6%), 7 g instant yeast (1.4%) and, after the gluten develops, 40 g soft butter (8%).
Total dough: 25 + 125 + 475 + 175 + 50 + 50 + 8 + 7 + 40 = 955 g, enough for two 450 g loaves in small tins with a little spare. Bake at about 175 C for 30 to 35 minutes, to about 88 to 90 C inside.
blocks.result: Folake's loaves stay soft for three days in a bag, a strong selling point for cafe customers who buy on Monday and serve through the week.

blocks.text: Baking and storing enriched bread

Sugar, milk and eggs brown quickly, so enriched breads bake at lower temperatures than lean bread. If the top darkens before the loaf is done inside, cover it loosely with foil. Brush hot loaves with melted butter or a light sugar syrup for a soft, shiny top. Cool completely before bagging, or trapped steam will make the crust wet and encourage mould. Most soft enriched breads without preservatives are best within 2 to 4 days; freezing sliced loaves keeps them longer.

blocks.title: Egg wash and hygiene
blocks.text: Raw egg wash should be made fresh, kept covered in the fridge between uses and thrown away at the end of the day. Use a clean brush, wash it in hot soapy water after use, and never brush egg onto bread that has already been baked.

blocks.title: Additives
blocks.text: Use only food-grade ingredients from known suppliers, and if you choose a bread improver, use a properly labelled, NAFDAC-registered product exactly as directed. Good technique, tangzhong and enrichment can give soft bread without relying on improvers.

takeaways: Enrichment softens crumb and crust but slows yeast.
Add brioche butter only after gluten is developed; keep dough cool.
Tangzhong is 1 part flour to 5 parts liquid cooked to about 65 C.
Bake enriched bread cooler and to about 88 to 90 C inside.

activity.title: Bake a tangzhong milk loaf
steps: Calculate a tangzhong for 5% of your total flour.
Cook it to 65 C and cool it.
Mix, rise, shape and bake a milk loaf, recording dough temperature and times.
Keep one slice in a bag and test its softness on days 1, 2 and 3.
activity.evidence: Your formula in grams and percentages, photos of the tangzhong and the sliced loaf, and your three-day softness notes.

quiz.q: A recipe uses 10 g instant yeast. Roughly how much fresh yeast would replace it?
quiz.explain: Fresh yeast is used at about 2.5 to 3 times the weight of instant yeast.

quiz.q: Target dough temperature 25 C, room 30 C, flour 29 C, friction 4 C. What water temperature is needed?
Dough smells strongly of alcohol, has collapsed and tears easily. What happened?
quiz.explain: These are the signs of over-fermentation, usually from warm dough, too much yeast or too long a rise.

quiz.q: Ladi needs 500 g baked loaves and her bake loss is 10%. About what should each dough piece weigh?
quiz.explain: 500 / 0.9 = about 556 g of dough to finish at 500 g after baking.

quiz.q: During the poke test the dent springs back quickly and completely. What should she do?
quiz.explain: A fast spring-back means the loaf is underproofed and needs more time.

quiz.q: When should butter be added to brioche dough?
options: At the very start with the flour
After the gluten is well developed, a little at a time
After baking, brushed on top only
quiz.explain: Fat blocks gluten formation, so brioche gluten is developed first and the butter worked in gradually.

quiz.q: For a tangzhong using 30 g flour, how much milk is needed at the usual ratio?
quiz.explain: Tangzhong is usually 1 part flour to 5 parts liquid: 30 x 5 = 150 g.

modules.title: Decoration, Celebration Cakes and the Business
modules.overview: The last module turns your skills into income. You will cover cakes with fondant and make simple sugar decorations safely, plan and engineer tiered celebration cakes with correct servings, and price, package and manage orders so every cake makes a real profit.

lessons.title: Fondant covering, modelling paste and sugar work
objectives: Prepare a cake with a firm base coat ready for fondant
Calculate the size of fondant needed and cover a cake with smooth sides
Turn fondant into modelling paste and make simple decorations
Handle fondant in humidity and hot sugar safely

blocks.text: Rolled **fondant** (also called sugar paste) is a pliable sugar dough rolled into a sheet and draped over a cake. It gives the smooth, porcelain look customers expect on many wedding and birthday cakes, and it protects the cake underneath. In a humid climate it needs careful handling, but once you understand it, fondant opens the door to the highest-priced cakes.

blocks.name: wedding
blocks.caption: Smooth fondant finishes are standard for many wedding and engagement cakes.

blocks.text: Prepare the base

Fondant shows every bump underneath it, so the cake must be smooth, straight and firm first. Cover it with firm ganache (2 : 1 dark or 3 : 1 white, from Module 2) or a firm buttercream, scraped sharp and chilled until hard. Just before covering, brush the surface very lightly with water or cooled boiled water if using ganache, or let a chilled buttercream lose its chill slightly so the fondant can stick.
How big to roll

The fondant circle must cover the top and both sides, plus a margin. The rule: **diameter of the top + 2 x height + about 5 cm**. Roll to about 4 to 5 mm thick on a surface dusted with cornflour or icing sugar, lifting and turning the sheet often so it does not stick. Thinner sheets tear; thicker sheets sag and crack at the edge.

blocks.title: Worked example: covering a 20 cm cake
blocks.context: For example, Ebere in Abakaliki is covering a 20 cm round cake that is 12 cm tall for an engagement.
steps: Rolled diameter: 20 + (2 x 12) + 5 = 49 cm. She marks 49 cm on her worktop with tape as a guide.
She kneads the fondant until warm and pliable, rolls it to 4 to 5 mm, and checks it reaches the tape on every side.
She lifts the sheet over her rolling pin, drapes it over the cake, and smooths the top first with a fondant smoother to push out air.
Working around the cake, she lifts and opens the skirt with one hand and smooths downwards with the other, so no pleats form.

She trims the excess with a sharp knife or pizza wheel, then weighs the trimmings: 1,150 g rolled, 330 g trimmed, so 820 g was used. She writes 820 g against 20 cm x 12 cm in her notes for future quotes.
blocks.result: A smooth covered cake, and an accurate fondant figure for this size so she can cost the next one exactly.

blocks.text: Modelling paste and decorations

Fondant alone is too soft for standing figures, bows or flower petals. Knead in a gum such as **CMC (also sold as tylose powder)**, usually around 1 level teaspoon per 250 g of fondant; follow the brand's instructions. Leave it wrapped for an hour or so to firm. Modelling paste rolls thinner and dries harder, so bows hold their shape and petals can be thin. Stick pieces together with a little edible glue (a pinch of CMC dissolved in water) and let decorations dry for a day or more before placing them.

blocks.title: Covering a cake in fondant
items: Firm, smooth base coat
Roll to 4 to 5 mm
Drape and smooth top
Open skirt, smooth sides
Trim and polish
blocks.caption: Most fondant problems come from a soft or uneven base coat in the first step.

blocks.text: Humidity and the fridge

Fondant attracts moisture. In humid weather it can become sticky, and a fondant cake taken from a cold fridge into warm air will **sweat**: water droplets form on the surface. Do not wipe them, which leaves marks. Leave the cake in its closed box at cool room temperature and let the moisture evaporate on its own, ideally with air conditioning or a fan moving air in the room. Store unused fondant tightly wrapped in an airtight container, not in the fridge.
Simple sugar work

Sugar work means shaping cooked sugar or **isomalt** (a sugar substitute that stays clear and resists humidity better) into gems, sails, shards and lace. It is heated far above boiling water, well past 150 C, and it sticks to skin while it burns.

blocks.title: Hot sugar and inedible decorations
blocks.text: Wear heat-resistant gloves for hot sugar, keep children and pets out of the kitchen, use a heavy pan on a stable burner, and keep a bowl of cold water nearby; if sugar touches skin, cool the area under cool running water for at least 20 minutes and seek medical help for serious burns. Never push wires, toothpicks, ribbon or fresh flower stems directly into cake: use a food-safe posy pick, tell the customer which parts are not edible, and use only flowers known to be safe and free from pesticides.

takeaways: Fondant needs a firm, smooth, chilled base coat.
Roll to top diameter + 2 x height + 5 cm, about 4 to 5 mm thick.
Add CMC to fondant for modelling paste that dries firm.
Let sweating fondant dry on its own; handle hot sugar with care.

lessons.title: Designing and engineering tiered celebration cakes
objectives: Run a design consultation and turn it into a written brief
Calculate servings from tier sizes and plan for the guest count
Support stacked tiers safely with boards and dowels
Plan delivery and set-up for a tiered cake

blocks.text: A celebration cake is a design project. The customer brings an occasion, a guest count, a budget and often a photo from social media. Your job is to turn that into a cake that looks right, feeds the right number of people, survives the journey and the heat, and makes you a profit. Good cake designers ask questions first and sketch second.

blocks.name: happy-birthday
blocks.caption: Every celebration cake starts with understanding the occasion and the guests.

blocks.text: The consultation checklist

items: Date, time, venue, and whether the venue is air conditioned or outdoors.
Number of guests to serve, and whether there will be other desserts.
Flavours, fillings and any allergies or dietary needs (for example nuts, eggs, dairy).
Colours, theme, inspiration photos, and any lettering with exact spelling.
Budget range, delivery or pickup, and set-up needs.

blocks.text: Write the answers into a short brief and send it back on WhatsApp for the customer to confirm in writing. Add a simple sketch with tier sizes and heights. When a customer sends a photo of a large cake but a small budget, show them what fits their budget: fewer tiers, a dummy tier, or simpler decoration.
Calculating servings

A widely used celebration serving is a slice about **2.5 cm wide by 5 cm deep**, cut from a tier about 10 cm tall. That footprint is 12.5 square centimetres. To estimate servings, divide the area of the tier top by 12.5. For a round tier, area is 3.14 x radius x radius. Real cutting of round cakes gives a little less than the theory, so take off about 10%.

blocks.title: Worked example: a 150-guest wedding cake
blocks.context: For example, a couple in Benin City wants three round tiers, 25 cm, 20 cm and 15 cm, each 10 cm tall, for 150 guests. The cake designer is Osas.
steps: 25 cm tier: radius 12.5; area = 3.14 x 12.5 x 12.5 = about 491 square cm; 491 / 12.5 = about 39 servings.
Total in theory: 39 + 25 + 14 = 78. Allowing 10% cutting loss: about 70 servings.
Shortfall: 150 - 70 = 80 servings. Osas offers a kitchen sheet cake of the same flavour, 30 x 40 cm, cut behind the scenes: 1,200 / 12.5 = 96 in theory, about 86 after allowing for edges.
Total: about 70 + 86 = 156 servings, enough for 150 guests while keeping the display cake the size the couple wanted.
blocks.result: Osas meets the guest count without building an oversized display cake, and the customer understands exactly why the sheet cake is needed.

blocks.text: Engineering stacked tiers

Cake is soft. Without support, a top tier sinks into the one below. Every tier sits on its own **cake board** the same size as the tier. Into each tier that carries weight, push **dowels** (food-safe plastic or wooden rods), commonly 4 to 6 per tier, in a circle a little inside the outline of the tier above. Mark each dowel at the exact height of the cake, pull it out, cut all of them to the same length, and push them back so the upper board rests on the dowels, not on the cake. For transport of tall cakes, many decorators also drive one long sharpened central dowel down through all the boards into the drum.

blocks.title: How a tiered cake carries weight
items: Top tier on its board
Middle tier, dowels, board
Base tier, dowels, board
Heavy cake drum
blocks.caption: Weight passes through boards and dowels down to the drum, not through the soft cake.

blocks.text: Delivery and set-up

items: Chill the finished cake so the coating is firm before moving it.
Use a sturdy box taller than the cake, on a non-slip mat, on a flat surface in the car, with the air conditioning on. Never on a seat or a lap.
Drive slowly over bumps; for very tall cakes, transport tiers separately and stack at the venue.
At the venue, check the table is level and out of direct sun, add final decorations, take photos, and get the client or coordinator to confirm the cake arrived in good condition.

blocks.text: Build in time as well as structure. A three-tier cake is usually baked two to three days before the event, filled and coated the next day, and decorated and stacked the day before delivery, so plan your calendar backwards from the delivery time and do not book two large tiered cakes for the same day until you have help.

blocks.title: Dummy tiers
blocks.text: A decorated polystyrene dummy tier gives height at lower cost. Tell the customer clearly which tiers are real and which are dummies, and price the decorating work on the dummy, which takes just as long.

takeaways: Turn every consultation into a written, confirmed brief.
Servings: tier area divided by 12.5, minus about 10% for rounds.
Each tier needs its own board and cut-to-height dowels below it.
Deliver chilled, boxed, flat and in a cool car.

lessons.title: Costing, pricing, packaging and managing orders
objectives: Cost a cake fully, including packaging, overheads and your labour
Set a price and explain the difference between markup and margin
Package and label cakes safely and attractively
Run orders with written confirmations, deposits and safe payment checks

blocks.text: Many skilled bakers stay busy but broke because they price by guessing or by copying competitors. A professional price covers every naira spent, pays you fairly for your time, and leaves a profit for growth. Ingredient prices in Nigeria change often, so you need a costing method you can update quickly, not a price list you set once.

blocks.name: receipt
blocks.caption: Write every cost down; prices you cannot see are prices you cannot charge for.

blocks.text: Five parts of a full cost

blocks.title: Building a price
items: Profit
Your labour
Overheads: gas, power, water
Packaging and boards
Ingredients
blocks.caption: Ingredients are only the base; a price that covers only ingredients loses money on every cake.

items: **Ingredients:** cost per gram from your receipts, multiplied by the grams used. Recheck prices every month.
**Packaging:** box, board, drum, ribbon, labels, candles if included.
**Overheads:** a share of gas or electricity, water, cleaning materials, data for WhatsApp, equipment wear.
**Labour:** the hours spent baking, decorating, shopping and delivering, multiplied by an hourly rate you decide.
**Profit:** a percentage added on top, for savings, new equipment and quiet months.

blocks.text: Cost per gram: the key habit

Divide what you paid for a pack by its weight in grams. That cost per gram, multiplied by the grams in your formula, gives the true cost of each ingredient. The prices below are assumed figures to show the method only; replace them with your own receipts.

Notice how butter, used in both the sponge and the buttercream, is by far the largest cost in this example. That is common for buttercream cakes and is why a price rise in butter should trigger an immediate review of your cake prices.

blocks.title: Worked example: pricing a 20 cm three-layer cake
blocks.context: For example, Hauwa in Abuja costs a 20 cm, three-layer vanilla cake with SMBC. The naira figures are assumptions for illustration only; use your own current market prices.
steps: Ingredients: the four main items from the table above come to 600 + 5,400 + 1,000 + 1,600 = N8,600. Milk, vanilla, jam and other small items add about N3,400, so ingredients total about N12,000.
Packaging: cake board, drum and box, about N3,500. Overheads share: about N2,000.
Labour: 5 hours at N1,500 per hour = N7,500.
She adds a 30% markup: 25,000 x 1.30 = N32,500.
Margin check: profit 32,500 - 25,000 = N7,500; 7,500 / 32,500 = about 23% of the selling price.
blocks.result: Hauwa's price is N32,500. She understands that a 30% markup on cost is only about a 23% margin on the price, so she never confuses the two when giving discounts.

blocks.title: Discounts eat profit fast
blocks.text: In Hauwa's example a 10% discount (N3,250) cuts her N7,500 profit by over 40%. Offer added value, like a free message plaque, before cutting the price.
Packaging and labelling

Use food-grade boxes that are taller and wider than the cake, with a window if possible. Put the cake on a board and a non-slip mat inside the box. Add a label or card with your business name and phone number, the product, the date made, storage advice such as keep refrigerated or keep cool and out of the sun, best eaten by date, and an **allergen list**, for example wheat (gluten), egg, milk, nuts. If you later sell packaged products through shops or supermarkets, check NAFDAC registration requirements and register your business name with the CAC.
Managing orders

items: Use a standard order form (on paper, Google Forms or WhatsApp Business) with the brief, price, delivery details and dates.
Send a written confirmation and ask for a deposit, often 50 to 70%, to book the date. State your cancellation and changes policy clearly.
Confirm every payment inside your bank app (for example on Opay, Moniepoint or your bank's app). Never accept a screenshot or a text alert as proof: fake alerts are a common scam.
Collect the balance before delivery or at pickup, and send a receipt.
Keep a weekly production calendar showing each order's baking, decorating and delivery day, so you never accept more than your oven and hours allow.

blocks.title: Customer data
blocks.text: Order forms hold names, phone numbers and addresses. Keep them private, do not post customer details or screenshots of chats without permission, and delete old details you no longer need.

takeaways: Cost ingredients, packaging, overheads, labour and profit.
Markup is on cost; margin is on price. 30% markup is about 23% margin.
Label cakes with storage advice and allergens.
Take deposits, confirm payments in your bank app, and plan capacity.

activity.title: Build your costing sheet
steps: List current prices for your main ingredients and work out a cost per gram for each.

quiz.q: Bimpe needs to cover a 15 cm round cake that is 10 cm tall. About what diameter should she roll the fondant?
quiz.explain: Top diameter + 2 x height + about 5 cm: 15 + 20 + 5 = 40 cm.

quiz.q: A fondant cake taken out of the fridge is covered in tiny water droplets. What should she do?
options: Wipe it dry with a cloth
Leave it in its closed box to dry on its own, with moving air
Put it back in the freezer
quiz.explain: Wiping marks the surface. Condensation evaporates on its own if left alone with good air flow.

quiz.q: What is the safe way to add fresh flowers or wired decorations to a cake?
options: Push the stems straight into the cake
Use a food-safe posy pick and tell the customer which parts are inedible
Glue them on with fondant only
Hide the wires inside the filling
quiz.explain: Posy picks keep stems and wires out of the cake, and customers must know what not to eat.

quiz.q: Using 12.5 square cm per serving, about how many theoretical servings does a 20 cm round tier give?
quiz.explain: Area = 3.14 x 10 x 10 = 314 square cm; 314 / 12.5 is about 25.

quiz.q: In a stacked cake, what actually carries the weight of the upper tiers?
options: Boards resting on dowels cut to the height of the tier below
quiz.explain: Weight passes through boards and dowels down to the drum, not through the soft cake.

quiz.q: A cake costs N20,000 in total. Joy adds a 25% markup. What is the price and profit margin?
A new customer sends a screenshot of a transfer for the deposit. What should the baker do before starting the cake?
options: Confirm the money has actually arrived in her bank app
Accept it because the customer seems friendly
quiz.explain: Screenshots and text alerts can be faked. Only an actual credit in the account confirms payment.

finalQuiz.q: A formula uses 1,200 g flour and 24 g salt. What is the salt in baker's percentages?
finalQuiz.explain: 24 / 1,200 = 0.02, so 2% of the flour weight, which is normal for bread.

finalQuiz.q: Which change will make a shortcrust more tender?
options: Rubbing in cold fat and using only enough water to bind
Adding extra water so it rolls easily
finalQuiz.explain: Fat coats the proteins and limited water and mixing keep gluten low, giving a short, tender pastry.

finalQuiz.q: Her oven runs 15 C hot and she bakes in a fan oven. A recipe says 180 C conventional. What dial setting is most sensible?
finalQuiz.explain: Fan ovens need about 20 C less (160 C), and her oven runs 15 C hot, so set the dial to about 145 C and check with the thermometer.

finalQuiz.q: Which sponge suits a layered cake that must be cut into thin, neat layers and soaked with syrup?
options: Chiffon baked in a tube tin
finalQuiz.explain: Genoise has a firm, fine crumb that slices thinly and is designed to be moistened with syrup.

finalQuiz.q: Why do professionals apply a thin crumb coat and chill it before the final coat?
options: To seal loose crumbs so the final coat is clean
finalQuiz.explain: The thin chilled coat traps crumbs so they do not show in the final finish.

finalQuiz.q: For a hot outdoor venue, which finish will hold sharp edges longest?
finalQuiz.explain: Firm ganache has a higher setting point and holds its shape in heat better than butter or cream finishes.

finalQuiz.q: Rough puff butter leaks out and fries in the tray, and the pastry barely rises. What is the most likely cause?
options: The oven was not hot enough when the pastry went in
finalQuiz.explain: In a cool oven the butter melts out before steam forms to lift the layers. Preheat fully to 200 to 220 C.

finalQuiz.q: Choux shells came out flat and spread. What should Lola change?
options: Add the last egg more slowly and stop when the V test passes
Open the oven door to release steam
finalQuiz.explain: Flat shells mean the paste was too runny, usually from too much egg.

finalQuiz.q: Dough target 26 C, room 32 C, flour 31 C, friction 5 C. Which water temperature should she use?
Which statement about enriched dough is correct?
options: It bakes hotter than lean bread
Sugar, eggs and milk brown quickly, so it bakes cooler, to about 88 to 90 C inside
Butter should go in at the start for best gluten
It needs less yeast than lean dough
finalQuiz.explain: Enriched dough browns fast, so it is baked at a lower temperature, and butter is added after gluten develops.

finalQuiz.q: A three-tier cake gives about 70 servings after the cutting allowance, but there are 120 guests. What is the most practical solution?
options: Cut every slice in half without telling anyone
Add a matching kitchen sheet cake for the extra servings
Remove the dowels to make room
Tell the client to invite fewer guests
finalQuiz.explain: A kitchen sheet cake in the same flavour supplies extra servings without changing the display design.

finalQuiz.q: Total cost is N40,000 and she wants a 25% profit margin on the selling price. Which price achieves that?
finalQuiz.explain: For a 25% margin, cost must be 75% of price: 40,000 / 0.75 = about N53,333. A 25% markup (N50,000) gives only a 20% margin.
